claims.text: The no-show fee is chargeable ONLY IF all four limbs of POL-NS-01 hold, and limb (b) requires the gps_trace to place the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at or before the 'arrived' event of 12:26:40. EV-GPS-00626 is MISSING: the admissibility pre-pass records issue MISSING_ARTIFACT — 'No driver telemetry was retained for this trip' — at weight_multiplier 0.0, so there is no trace at all. No fix of any accuracy places the driver anywhere, let alone inside the pickup geofence, and the driver's conjunctive burden fails at limb (b).

POL-NS-02 is express on these facts: where the gps_trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix at any point in the 15 minutes preceding the cancellation, the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a FULL REFUND of the cancellation fee. EV-GPS-00626 contains no fix at all — I cite that absence and disclose in the same breath that the artifact is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0 — so the clause's condition is satisfied and the SGD 4.00 charged to the rider at 12:36:00 must be returned.

Limb (c) of POL-NS-01 deliberately runs the dwell clock from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and NOT from the driver's 'arrived' tap. The trip record's wait_time_min of 9.0 and arrived_at of 12:26:40 are therefore not the statutory dwell; with EV-GPS-00626 missing there is no qualifying fix from which any dwell can start, so the driver's case fails at (c) as well as at (b).

The driver's own statement on the record is that he had gone offline for a break, that the app 'must have kept me online', that he did not see the booking until the rider called, and that he 'never accepted it knowingly' — the account of a driver who was not at the pickup attending a waiting rider. The trip telemetry corroborates it: the rider's in-app call at 12:25:40 went unanswered, and the driver's only in-app call was placed at 12:32:40, six minutes after the 'arrived' marker he is said to have tapped at 12:26:40.

EV-ADVIS-00626-01 is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) — no advisory covers the pickup road in this window. POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits separated in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a present and populated advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covers the pickup road, and it makes the limb unavailable against a MISSING advisory. The driver therefore has no advisory route by which any gap in his in-geofence presence could be patched.

POL-NS-07 compensates the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. Limb (b) is not satisfied on this record (no trace, no in-radius fix), so the SGD 3.20 driver-compensation figure the ledger computes has no predicate and no compensation is payable out of the rider's SGD 4.00.

I concede one point rather than stretch it: EV-CHAT-00626 is COMPLETE and holds zero messages, so the rider sent no locating or coordinating message and POL-NS-04 is not available on this record. The rider's case does not need it. The empty log is equally no evidence that the rider was absent, and it supplies no reply from the driver anywhere in the waiting window.

Even on the reading most generous to the driver — that the missing trace leaves the arrival fact unsettled rather than decided against him — the rider still does not carry the disputed charge. POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at the minimum weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, and the only artifact bearing on arrival here is the missing trace at 0.0, below the platform-wide 0.70 floor; POL-NS-09 then sends the case to a human reviewer with the SGD 4.00 placed on hold rather than collected. Escalation and full refund both leave the fee off the rider.

claims.text: The platform's own trip record for TRP-00626 — admissible at weight 1.0 with no issues — carries a driver 'arrived' event at 12:26:40, six minutes after the 12:20:40 acceptance. POL-NS-01 limb (a) is therefore satisfied on the record, not on assertion.

The same record terminates the trip at 12:35:40 by the driver's own action under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes POL-NS-01 limb (d) recognises — with no boarding event and no DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE code anywhere in the record. Limb (d) is satisfied.

On the record's own clock the driver held station from the logged arrival at 12:26:40 to the cancellation at 12:35:40: 540 seconds, which the trip record itself reports as wait_time_min 9.0, comfortably above the 300-second STANDARD minimum carried by the fee schedule for the STANDARD zone class the fare ledger publishes for this trip. The only admissible measure of the dwell on this bundle is 9 minutes, not 3.

The GPS trace is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and I disclose it as such. That cuts for the driver, not against him: a missing artifact can carry no fact, so no admissible artifact in this bundle places the driver outside the arrival radius or fixes his speed at the arrival marker, and the rider's narrative that he 'just stopped somewhere' has nothing in the evidence behind it. POL-NS-08's own drafting states that a trace too poor to establish in-radius readings is impairment rather than proof of absence; the same reasoning applies with greater force where no trace was retained at all. The trace-dependent clauses cannot be run affirmatively against the driver.

POL-NS-04 cannot exculpate the rider. Its limb (a) requires a rider message in the chat log that is locating or coordinating, and the chat export for this trip holds zero messages (message_count 0, messages []), matching trip_record.chat_message_count 0 — so there is no message to hang the clause on. Limb (b) fails independently on the same record: the driver placed an in-app call at 12:32:40 that was answered (40 seconds), before he terminated the trip at 12:35:40. A clause that requires both limbs to hold cannot apply where neither does.

Nothing establishes a false arrival marker under POL-NS-05. There is no trace to place the driver more than 300 m from the pin, or in motion at 15 km/h or above, at the 12:26:40 arrival timestamp, and the record is internally consistent on its face: arrival is logged exactly 6.0 minutes after acceptance (12:20:40 to 12:26:40), which is precisely the time_to_arrival_min 6.0 the trip record states for this booking. A marker that matches the platform's own quoted time-to-arrival is not a false marker.

POL-NS-06's shortfall route is also unavailable. The effective dwell on the only admissible evidence is the recorded 9-minute wait, which exceeds the 300-second STANDARD minimum rather than falling short of it. I disclose that limb (i) accumulation cannot be invoked on the driver's side either, because the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00626-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — but limb (i) only permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed, and on a 9-minute continuous hold no summing is required.

The ledger reconciles with the fee schedule, so no integrity defect arises under POL-NS-08(d): the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee charged equals the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The rider disputes SGD 4.00 and the ledger line is exactly SGD 4.00.

POL-NS-07's anti-farming check passes on both of its limbs, and I cite only the two fields that clause names: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 110 is 0.009, below the 0.08 rate. Compensation is therefore not withheld, and the driver's entitlement is 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee — SGD 3.20 — the figure the fare ledger's own derived money block computes at clause POL-NS-07.

No profile-based escalation trigger fires on this bundle: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, well short of the 2 that POL-NS-09(c) requires, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, far short of the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires. With the fee still CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, the state the evidence supports is the present state: on a rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION leaves the charge standing, and that is the disposition the driver asks for.

ruling.explanation:
This case goes to a human reviewer, and the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is placed on hold — neither collected from the rider nor refunded — while review is pending. Here is why, for both of you.

WHAT IS SETTLED. The charge turns on POL-NS-01, which is conjunctive: the SGD 4.00 fee stands only if all four limbs hold. Limb (a) — a driver 'arrived' event in the trip record — is satisfied on the platform's own record (12:26:40). Limb (d) — no boarding, terminated by the driver under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — is satisfied (cancelled_at 12:35:40). Those two limbs are decided in the driver's favour.

WHAT IS NOT SETTLED. Limbs (b) and (c) are read off the GPS trace. Limb (b) requires the trace to place the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at or before 12:26:40; limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, expressly NOT from the 'arrived' tap. EV-GPS-00626 is MISSING: the admissibility pre-pass records issue MISSING_ARTIFACT at weight_multiplier 0.0 — 'No driver telemetry was retained for this trip.' There is no GPS evidence at all.

RIDER'S ARGUMENT (limb (b) fails, POL-NS-02 full refund): REJECTED. An absent trace is the limiting case of an impaired one, and POL-NS-08(b) makes a trace with fewer than six fixes across the waiting window impaired. POL-NS-02's 'no qualifying in-radius fix' rule addresses a trace that was kept and shows the driver elsewhere; the clause's own note says a trace too poor to support the arrival test is impairment rather than proof of absence, and that applies with more force where no trace was kept. Limbs (b) and (c) are therefore UNDECIDED — not proof the driver arrived, and not proof he did not. An undecided limb supports neither a payment that needs the clause to hold nor a refund that needs it to fail.

DRIVER'S ARGUMENTS: (1) The recorded wait of 9.0 minutes (12:26:40 to 12:35:40, wait_time_min 9.0) is REJECTED as the statutory dwell: limb (c) runs the clock from GPS geofence entry, not from the driver's tap. (2) The missing trace cannot be run affirmatively against the driver — accepted as far as it goes, but it cuts both ways: the same absence means the fee cannot be carried either. (3) The driver's counterparty statement ('I had gone offline for a break… I never accepted it knowingly') is an admission against his own interest that he was not attending the pickup, and it leaves the 12:26:40 'arrived' marker unexplained; it does not, however, supply the GPS position the limbs require. (4) POL-NS-04 does not apply — the chat log is COMPLETE but empty, and the driver's in-app call at 12:32:40 was answered — and the rider correctly concedes this. (5) POL-NS-06 limb (i) is unavailable because the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00626-01 is MISSING. (6) POL-NS-07 compensation of SGD 3.20 (80% of SGD 4.00) is REJECTED: it is payable only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied IN FULL, and limb (b) is not; the anti-farming check itself passes (no_show_terminations_30d 1, 1/110 = 0.009, below both thresholds of 4 and 0.08), which clears the withholding branch but creates no entitlement. So is the POL-NS-03 pin-ambiguity goodwill of SGD 2.00 — the 400 m stationary test cannot be run without a trace.

LEDGER AND INTEGRITY. No POL-NS-08(d) defect: the SGD 4.00 charged equals the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

WHY ESCALATE. The only evidence that could decide arrival is the missing trace at weight 0.0. POL-NS-08 so provides (ruling may not exceed PARTIAL_REFUND, case escalates under POL-NS-09), POL-NS-09(e) fires because the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired, and POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at 0.0 — below the 0.70 floor — engaging POL-NS-09(a) as well. Escalation is terminal and replaces the money outcome. The profile triggers do not fire (disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 for both parties under POL-NS-09(c); rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 under POL-NS-09(d)). No clause produces a referral on these facts.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE REVIEWER: obtain the driver telemetry for TRP-00626 (or other evidence of the driver's position between 12:26:40 and 12:35:40) and determine whether he was inside the 50 m STANDARD radius for a continuous 300-second dwell. If he was, the SGD 4.00 stands and POL-NS-07 compensation may follow; if he was not, or the trace genuinely does not exist, decide the fee on the balance of the remaining evidence, noting the driver's own admission that he was offline and did not knowingly accept the trip.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver: you are reading the same gap in the evidence in opposite directions, and neither reading can be reached on this record.

The uncontested facts are these. The trip record shows a driver 'arrived' event at 12:26:40, six minutes after the 12:20:40 acceptance, and the driver ended the trip at 12:35:40 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the codes POL-NS-01 limb (d) recognises. The fare ledger shows SGD 4.00 charged to the rider at 12:36:00 with SGD 0.00 refunded, and that figure reconciles with the fee schedule, which fixes the charge as the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) — so there is no billing-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d).

What the record does not contain is any location data. The GPS trace was never retained: EV-GPS-00626 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT. The traffic advisory is missing for the same reason: EV-ADVIS-00626-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT.

POL-NS-01 lets a no-show fee stand only if all four of its conditions hold, and the driver must carry every one. Two of them read the GPS trace: limb (b), which needs the trace to place the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD pickup geofence at or before the arrival event, and limb (c), which needs a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least 300 seconds measured from the first qualifying GPS fix — not from the 'arrived' tap and not from the trip record's wait_time_min. With no trace, those two limbs are neither satisfied nor broken. They are undecided, and an undecided limb supports neither the charge nor the refund.

That is why I cannot grant the rider a full refund on the argument that 'no trace means he never arrived.' POL-NS-02 reaches a full refund where the trace contains no qualifying in-radius fix, but the policy is explicit that a defective trace is evidence of impairment rather than proof of absence, and an absent trace is the limiting case of a defective one. And it is why I cannot let the SGD 4.00 stand, or pay the driver, on the argument that the trip record's 9.0-minute wait_time_min proves the required dwell: limb (c) deliberately runs the clock from the GPS fix, so the record alone cannot carry that fact.

The driver's compensation claim therefore fails at its own gate. POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80 percent of the fee — SGD 3.20 of SGD 4.00 — only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not. The anti-farming check POL-NS-07 names does pass (no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 110 is 0.009, below 0.08), but that check only gates a compensation that has no predicate here. The rider's alternative routes are unavailable too: POL-NS-04 does not apply because the chat log holds zero messages and the driver placed an answered in-app call at 12:32:40, and POL-NS-06 limb (i) cannot be invoked because it requires a present and populated advisory, and EV-ADVIS-00626-01 is missing. No profile-based escalation trigger fires either: disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 — so the escalation is not about abuse on either side.

The one fact this whole dispute turns on — whether the driver was at the pickup and waited the required time — is carried only by an artifact that was not retained. Confidence is therefore capped at 0.0, far below the platform-wide floor of 0.70, and the case goes to a human reviewer under POL-NS-09(a) and POL-NS-09(e). The SGD 4.00 is held: it is neither collected nor refunded while the review is pending.

The specific question for the reviewer: whether a driver 'arrived' event at 12:26:40 with a recorded 9-minute wait can stand as a verified rider no-show when no GPS trace was retained to test the arrival, and why the trace for this trip is missing at all.

The trip record's wait_time_min of 9.0 and arrived_at of 12:26:40 are therefore not the statutory dwell; with EV-GPS-00626 missing there is no qualifying fix from which any dwell can start, so the driver's case fails at (c) as well as at (b).
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-GPS-00626 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: The driver's own statement on the record is that he had gone offline for a break, that the app 'must have kept me online', that he did not see the booking until the rider called, and that he 'never accepted it knowingly' — the account of a driver who was not at the pickup attending a waiting rider. The trip telemetry corroborates it: the rider's in-app call at 12:25:40 went unanswered, and the driver's only in-app call was placed at 12:32:40, six minutes after the 'arrived' marker he is said to have tapped at 12:26:40.

EV-ADVIS-00626-01 is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) — no advisory covers the pickup road in this window. POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits separated in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a present and populated advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT covers the pickup road, and it makes the limb unavailable against a MISSING advisory. The driver therefore has no advisory route by which any gap in his in-geofence presence could be patched.

POL-NS-07 compensates the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. Limb (b) is not satisfied on this record (no trace, no in-radius fix), so the SGD 3.20 driver-compensation figure the ledger computes has no predicate and no compensation is payable out of the rider's SGD 4.00.

I concede one point rather than stretch it: EV-CHAT-00626 is COMPLETE and holds zero messages, so the rider sent no locating or coordinating message and POL-NS-04 is not available on this record. The rider's case does not need it. The empty log is equally no evidence that the rider was absent, and it supplies no reply from the driver anywhere in the waiting window.

Even on the reading most generous to the driver — that the missing trace leaves the arrival fact unsettled rather than decided against him — the rider still does not carry the disputed charge. POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at the minimum weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, and the only artifact bearing on arrival here is the missing trace at 0.0, below the platform-wide 0.70 floor; POL-NS-09 then sends the case to a human reviewer with the SGD 4.00 placed on hold rather than collected. Escalation and full refund both leave the fee off the rider.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-GPS-00626 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: The platform's own trip record for TRP-00626 — admissible at weight 1.0 with no issues — carries a driver 'arrived' event at 12:26:40, six minutes after the 12:20:40 acceptance. POL-NS-01 limb (a) is therefore satisfied on the record, not on assertion.

The same record terminates the trip at 12:35:40 by the driver's own action under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three codes POL-NS-01 limb (d) recognises — with no boarding event and no DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE code anywhere in the record. Limb (d) is satisfied.

On the record's own clock the driver held station from the logged arrival at 12:26:40 to the cancellation at 12:35:40: 540 seconds, which the trip record itself reports as wait_time_min 9.0, comfortably above the 300-second STANDARD minimum carried by the fee schedule for the STANDARD zone class the fare ledger publishes for this trip. The only admissible measure of the dwell on this bundle is 9 minutes, not 3.

The GPS trace is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and I disclose it as such. That cuts for the driver, not against him: a missing artifact can carry no fact, so no admissible artifact in this bundle places the driver outside the arrival radius or fixes his speed at the arrival marker, and the rider's narrative that he 'just stopped somewhere' has nothing in the evidence behind it. POL-NS-08's own drafting states that a trace too poor to establish in-radius readings is impairment rather than proof of absence; the same reasoning applies with greater force where no trace was retained at all. The trace-dependent clauses cannot be run affirmatively against the driver.

POL-NS-04 cannot exculpate the rider. Its limb (a) requires a rider message in the chat log that is locating or coordinating, and the chat export for this trip holds zero messages (message_count 0, messages []), matching trip_record.chat_message_count 0 — so there is no message to hang the clause on. Limb (b) fails independently on the same record: the driver placed an in-app call at 12:32:40 that was answered (40 seconds), before he terminated the trip at 12:35:40. A clause that requires both limbs to hold cannot apply where neither does.

Nothing establishes a false arrival marker under POL-NS-05. There is no trace to place the driver more than 300 m from the pin, or in motion at 15 km/h or above, at the 12:26:40 arrival timestamp, and the record is internally consistent on its face: arrival is logged exactly 6.0 minutes after acceptance (12:20:40 to 12:26:40), which is precisely the time_to_arrival_min 6.0 the trip record states for this booking. A marker that matches the platform's own quoted time-to-arrival is not a false marker.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-GPS-00626 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: POL-NS-06's shortfall route is also unavailable. The effective dwell on the only admissible evidence is the recorded 9-minute wait, which exceeds the 300-second STANDARD minimum rather than falling short of it. I disclose that limb (i) accumulation cannot be invoked on the driver's side either, because the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00626-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — but limb (i) only permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed, and on a 9-minute continuous hold no summing is required.

The ledger reconciles with the fee schedule, so no integrity defect arises under POL-NS-08(d): the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee charged equals the GREATER of the STANDARD zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The rider disputes SGD 4.00 and the ledger line is exactly SGD 4.00.

POL-NS-07's anti-farming check passes on both of its limbs, and I cite only the two fields that clause names: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 110 is 0.009, below the 0.08 rate. Compensation is therefore not withheld, and the driver's entitlement is 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee — SGD 3.20 — the figure the fare ledger's own derived money block computes at clause POL-NS-07.

No profile-based escalation trigger fires on this bundle: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, well short of the 2 that POL-NS-09(c) requires, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, far short of the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires. With the fee still CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, the state the evidence supports is the present state: on a rider-filed dispute NO_ACTION leaves the charge standing, and that is the disposition the driver asks for.
